names.note: The calendar’s own name page for him is «Михаил (Якунькин), мч.»; the rank is stripped and the surname kept, the day line itself giving only «… Михаила». `fk.mjs` on the stored string returns NONE, and the two other Michaels this same day brings are «Кобзев» and the son of the 1918 line.

death.note: The year the day line closes with, «(1937)», which is the whole of what the source gives; no year of birth anywhere.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 10 декабря ст. ст. — «Сщмчч. Анатолия, Александра, Евгения, Константина, Николая пресвитеров, и с ними мчч. Петра, Евсевия, Михаила, Дорофея, Лаврентия, Григория и мцц. Александры и Татианы (1937).»

attestations.note: Eighth of the thirteen one line enumerates, and the third of the six laymen. THE LINE AND THE NAME PAGE ARE ALL THERE IS for him. THREE MICHAELS STAND ON THIS ONE DAY and the surnames are what tell them apart: this man «Якунькин», a layman of 1937; «Кобзев», an archpriest of 1937 on a line of his own; and the son of the 1918 line, whose name page carries a typographical fault for «Плетнев». `related` is left empty for the whole company, as the corpus leaves it for the thirty-four of Valaam. `new-martyr` is written as this corpus writes it for this calendar’s twentieth-century entries. No folder held him: a Cyrillic grep for «Якунькин» over every `saint.json` returns nothing. The day page prints eleven hymns and none is under any of the thirteen names.
